title: Stepwise upgrade playbook for private control plane (canary-first)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a repeatable, IaC-driven playbook and automation for upgrading Private/VPC control planes with a canary-first approach. The goal is to minimize blast radius, provide fast rollback, and push upgrades via Terraform modules + orchestration jobs that gate promotion based on health signals and smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: A documented upgrade playbook that runs from a CI job and is executable by SRE/Platform
Terraform modules and pipelines to create a canary control plane and pivot traffic to it automatically
Automated health gating: health probes, metrics thresholds, and synthetic smoke tests defined in the repo
Rollback triggers implemented: failed smoke tests, increased 5xxs, latency regressions beyond SLOs
Audit logs produced for each upgrade execution (who, when, from-commit, to-version)
Canary-to-production promotion automated with a configurable promotion window and cohort sizing
proposal: Introduce a 'stepwise' upgrade flow implemented as a set of Terraform modules and orchestrator jobs. The flow: 1) provision ephemeral canary control plane in target VPC using a versioned module; 2) sync configuration and run migration smoke tests (API, auth, webhook, RBAC); 3) run synthetic workloads and observe telemetry; 4) if green, promote a small percentage of customers (cohort) via routing config; 5) progressively increase cohort size while running targeted regression checks; 6) after full promotion, decommission old control plane. Rollback hooks will revert routing and optionally restore state from snapshot if database migrations are incompatible.
tasks: Design Terraform module versioning strategy and module inputs for canary provisioning
Add CI pipeline job to provision ephemeral canary control plane and run smoke tests
Define a minimal smoke test suite (API health, auth flow, leader election, webhook invocation)
Implement metric thresholds and alerting rules used as gating signals
Create traffic-slicing routing manifest and implement promotion CLI in deployer
Instrument audit events for upgrade operations in control plane control plane-audit log
Document operational runbook for manual interventions and emergency rollback
Run internal dry-run upgrades in staging and validate end-to-end timing and failure modes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry-run on staging clusters (non-customer). Phase 1: Single isolated canary customer in a non-production VPC. Phase 2: Internal canary (R&D teams) across 3 VPCs. Phase 3: Cohorted production promotion 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with 30m/1h observation windows. Each phase requires green smoke tests and no high-severity alerts. Promotion is automated but requires human "approver" for each major step in the first two executions.
health_checks: API server liveness & readiness for all replicas
Leader election stability and controller-manager reconciliation loop time
Webhook success rate and latency (95th percentile)
KV cache warmup time and hit ratio
Control-plane error rate (5xx) per minute compared to baseline
Token/KMS decryption success rate and TLS cert validation for endpoints
telemetry_requirements: Baseline latency and error percentiles for each control plane component prior to upgrade
Synthetic transaction traces for core flows (create job, list models, auth check)
Dashboard showing cohort-level KPIs and canary vs baseline diffs
Audit trail with commit hash of operator/runtime image used for canary
Automated Slack/PagerDuty notifications for gating failures
rollback_strategy: If any gating signal breaches thresholds during canary or cohort phases, the pipeline will automatically: 1) pause promotion, 2) revert routing to previous control plane, 3) run rollback smoke tests, 4) open incident with escalation. For incompatible DB migrations, the pipeline will block and require a manual migration plan; in that case the canary will be torn down and the run marked failed. All rollbacks must be recorded and include snapshot identifiers where state restoration was performed.
notes: We must ensure Terraform state separation between canary and production control planes to avoid accidental destroy of production state.
Operator API compatibility matrix needs a gate; verify that new operator images support old CRDs or include migration hooks.
Coordinate with Security for KMS key rotation windows when agents test decryption during canary runs.
Time-of-day scheduling: prefer off-peak windows for production promotions and provide blackout calendar for customers.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: DB schema changes that are not backwards compatible. Mitigation: require zero-downtime migration design or block promotion until manual migration is performed.
Risk: Terraform drift between environments causing provisioning failures. Mitigation: run preflight drift checks and fail fast with clear remediation steps.
Risk: Canary passes synthetic tests but fails with real traffic pattern. Mitigation: start with small customer cohort (5%) and use traffic replay where possible.
Risk: Secrets/KMS misconfiguration in canary. Mitigation: reuse customer KMS policies via IAM roles and run a key access verification step before promotion.
